handoff: 5 blocking: run cancel non-holder loosening not covered by slice 12 (F1); observe writes .norn-unit (F2, H2); round_migrate commit drop missing from legacyAction (F3, O5); AC6 uncommitted untested (F4); AC5 detached-check tick not staged (F5). Other skips verified against slices 10/11/13/14. e2e 71 pass/2 skip.

findings.title: Cross-clone run cancel loosened to exit 3 with no slice that restores it
findings.detail:
Before: refused(r, 'not_holder', 'norn story checkout gh-5'). Now: expect(r.exit).toBe(3). The non-holder is refused with `unknown_unit` and do_instead `norn status` (resolveUnit in run-cancel.ts:26 fails before the claim check at :30), so the B53 'held by X; checkout' message is gone. The comment names gh-195/12, but slice 12's AC1–AC5 cover only `story view` and `status` (B10, B13, B17–B19, B30); no criterion there or in any other slice covers run cancel or not_holder. The supervisor's ruling accepts a temporary loosening only when the named slice's criteria restore it.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Check the claim before resolveUnit in run-cancel.ts (claimFor needs only the story key) so the refusal stays not_holder, and restore the original assertion. Or have the person add a criterion to slice 12 and say so in the comment.

findings.title: Observe writes .norn-unit (an effect outside act and the trace)
findings.detail:
`if (inferred) writeUnitMarker(w.path, (marker = inferred));`. H2 says observe collects facts; effects belong to act and are traced (H4, P6). The write is not in the trace, so `run view --why` cannot account for it, and it runs inside observe rather than as a decided action. AC2 only needs the unit to be read again after git clean.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use the inferred marker in memory in observe, and restore the file in act (an action decide emits, or as part of an existing worktree-repair action).

findings.title: round_migrate dropped `commit` without a legacyAction entry
findings.detail:
RoundMigrateAction lost `commit: BoundaryCommit` (actions.ts ~360), but legacyAction (O5: reads a decision an older norn recorded) does not drop `commit` from an old round_migrate. The header's 'traces written by an older norn' note does not mention it either. Replaying an older trace's round.migrate with --why will show a difference.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: In legacyAction, drop `commit` from kind round_migrate. Update the header. Add a unit case that replays an old round_migrate decision.

findings.title: AC6 'uncommitted counts only the agent's files and the handoff' is UNTRACED
findings.detail:
AC6: 'the `uncommitted` fact counts only the agent's files and the handoff'. D8: 'covers the handoff and the agent's files only'. No test asserts uncommitted. The code counts only the handoff: a dirty agent file does not set it, and a dirty run-state file cannot appear. That may be the right reading, since counting the agent's files would fire recover.commit (story.ts:331) during a live session, but it is untested and differs from the AC wording. The facts.ts:159 comment still says 'runs/<unit>/ or handoff.md'.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Add a test at the agreed seam (S1 integration, or a decide unit case over the fact): uncommitted is true for a dirty handoff and false for a dirty machine-dir run-state file. If agent files are meant to be excluded, note that and update facts.ts:159; otherwise include them.

findings.title: AC5's tick during a detached check's receipt write is only inferred
findings.detail:
AC5: '(including a tick taken while a detached check run is writing its receipt), the next tick re-applies the receipt (S6)'. The spec's risk note: 'The tracer slice's test should pack in the middle of a check.' The test only checks that gh-9 ended at $done with pass and that a -check.json exists. No tick is shown to run between the check receipt landing and its state.json update. The crash test at :234 likewise relies on the ordinary gap after `norn done`, not a crash.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Stage it deterministically. Write a check receipt into the machine dir, with state.json not yet advanced, while the check's run is still listed as running; tick; assert the receipt is applied once and applied_through advances. Optionally do the same for a receipt with no state write.

findings.title: Golden --update changed more than record paths and commit path lists
findings.detail:
AC7 allows 'changes only in UnitFacts.record paths and commit path lists'. base-sync-dfbef4e59f1e and base-sync-ed107c7b9295 changed run_check.log_path. rebase-rewind-beb167688391 changed a noop reason (story.ts:291 dropped 'runs/ rewound'). Both are justified by S12 and small. The 20 harvested cases are additions only.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Name these two extra kinds of change in the PR, or have the person accept them at the gate.

findings.title: B34 flat-record tests now stage a flat record in the machine dir, which no norn writes
findings.detail:
The 'flat record from an older norn' setup used to commit a flat record on the branch. It now renames files inside the machine dir, a layout no norn version produces. The real older-norn case (flat record on the branch) is untested here. That is accepted as gh-195/06's job, and slice 06 was correctly not built. round_migrate is dormant until 06.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Say in the test that this exercises only round_migrate's mechanics until gh-195/06 brings back the on-branch case.

findings.title: story start remaking a removed worktree goes through checkoutStory's side effects
findings.detail:
Required by AC3 (judged in scope). It reuses checkoutStory, which appends a self-take receipt and a trace event. It covers the story worktree only, not a slice worktree (B3 says 'a unit's worktree'). worktreeGone is checked before waitForTickLock, and readLocalClaim(...).catch(() => null) treats a git error as 'no claim' silently.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Repeat the check under the tick lock; let the catch surface or trace the error; state in the slice or PR that slice worktrees are out of scope, or cover them.

findings.title: Weak assertions in the new AC tests
findings.detail:
AC2: the counters are empty, so 'same counters' passes trivially. AC4: 'the others are not' is checked on gh-9, which is already $done. AC3: the attempt is checked in state.json, not in `norn status` as the AC says. AC6: only Norn-Story and Norn-Step are asserted, not the other S4 trailers. S3 test: nothing asserts that _story is untouched by the slice reports. test/support/run-state.ts derives expected paths from the production resolver; only AC1 (:104) pins a literal path.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: Give gh-10 a non-zero counter before git clean, use a running unit as the 'other', read the attempt from `status --json`, and assert the full trailer set.

findings.title: Claim-race take-receipt check runs only when A wins
findings.detail:
`if (ra.exit === 0) { ... }`: when C wins, nothing is asserted about the take receipt. The comment names gh-195/10–11, which is acceptable under the ruling, but it is a conditional assertion in a race test.
Axis: spec
Suggestion: When gh-195/10–11 restore it, make the check unconditional.

findings.title: Handoff path built by hand; worktree folder naming duplicated
findings.detail:
`${story.spec_dir}/${unitHandoffPath(u.unit.dir)}` sits beside store's handoffPath, the one resolver. The `<repo>-worktrees/<id>-<slug>` naming now lives in story-start.ts:40, worktree.ts:93 (inferUnitMarker) and scanWorktrees (worktree.ts:138).
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Use the resolver and storyWorktreePath or scanWorktrees.

findings.title: Mechanical rewrite leftovers
findings.detail:
About 23 test imports end in a trailing comma, e.g. `import { repoConfigPath, workflowsDir, } from "@norn/store";`. Pure aliases: runStateDirIn = unitDir (run-state.ts:440) and oldRunnerLogDir = machineRunsDir (:308). normalRecord builds a RegExp per call (ids.ts:157). The transcript normaliser regex `/\brepos\/([\w.-]+?)-[0-9a-f]{8}\b/` is lazy; anchoring it to the end of the segment is safer.
Axis: standards
Suggestion: Clean up when touching these files.
